purpose: Reusable prompt patches for Rabbi video content generation, camera planning, platform ratios, Jewish thematic visuals, and publishing guardrails.

patches.title: One Time / Rabbi Scope
patches.apply_when: Always for Rabbi Elie Scheller or One Time Mishnah Class video content.
prompt_lines: The content is for One Time Mishnah Class with Rabbi Elie Scheller.
Frame the product as Mishnayos learning, Torah class prep, parent/student learning support, source sheets, worksheets, and family/community engagement.
Keep BNA private students, BNA accounting, BNA devices, and operator-only Changelog details out of the video prompt.
Use Bnei Neviim / BNA context only for shared production workflow, warm Torah-learning tone, and technical style guidance.
Do not imply this is a full-day BNA school video unless the source context explicitly says so.
negative_prompt_lines: No private BNA student names or accountability records.
No fake testimonials from parents or students.
No claim that Rabbi Elie has approved a final public message unless approval is provided.

patches.title: Privacy, Claims, And Torah Review
patches.apply_when: Always for public or semi-public Rabbi video output.
prompt_lines: Use only facts supplied in the source context or project memory.
If a Torah source, halacha point, or hashkafa claim is central to the clip, mark it for source-sheet/Rabbi review before publishing.
Do not present generated text as psak, a direct quote, or a named source unless the source is provided.
Avoid medical, educational-outcome, financial, or guaranteed-transformation promises.
Keep parent/student privacy intact; use archetypes like a boy, a parent, a chavrusa, or a family unless names are explicitly approved.
negative_prompt_lines: No invented pesukim, masechta references, page numbers, quotes, program outcomes, prices, dates, or enrollment claims.
No sensitive child struggles as public spectacle.

patches.title: 9:16 Vertical Short
patches.apply_when: Use for Reels, Shorts, WhatsApp status, TikTok-style clips, and most organic short-form output.
prompt_lines: Target 9:16 vertical video at 1080x1920.
Keep faces, sefarim, Hebrew text, and captions inside a center-safe crop; leave top and bottom breathing room for platform UI.
Use large readable text overlays, no more than 6 words per screen unless they are captions.
Prefer 18-30 seconds unless the operator gives a different duration.
Use close-up and medium shots more than wide shots, because vertical framing needs strong subject focus.
negative_prompt_lines: Do not place key captions at the extreme top or bottom.
Do not rely on tiny Hebrew text as the only message.

patches.title: 16:9 YouTube / Lesson Preview
patches.apply_when: Use for YouTube previews, course library clips, website video headers, and longer lesson excerpts.
prompt_lines: Target 16:9 horizontal video at 1920x1080.
Use wider establishing shots, desk/table context, and enough negative space for a title or source reference.
Keep the Rabbi, sefer, and topic readable without overcropping.
Use lower-third source/title graphics rather than large center captions.
Maintain a calm lesson-preview rhythm rather than a hyperactive social reel pace.
negative_prompt_lines: Do not crop the sefer or speaker hands out of the lesson context.
Do not use vertical-only framing instructions.

patches.title: 1:1 / 4:5 Feed Ad Candidate
patches.apply_when: Use for Facebook/Instagram/LinkedIn feed ad candidates or static-video hybrids.
prompt_lines: Target a feed-safe square or 4:5 composition.
Keep a clear headline zone, a subject zone, and a small CTA/source zone.
Use fewer shots than the vertical version; favor one strong idea and one clear visual anchor.
Make the first frame meaningful as a thumbnail.
negative_prompt_lines: Do not make the frame visually crowded.
Do not shrink the main Torah object or speaker until it becomes decorative.

patches.title: Learning Sequence Camera Coverage
patches.apply_when: Use for organic clips, ad candidates, and class/storytelling scenes.
prompt_lines: Build a camera sequence, not one static frame.
Start with an establishing shot of the learning table, room, beis midrash, or home-learning setup.
Cut to a medium shot of Rabbi Elie teaching or guiding.
Use an over-the-shoulder angle looking at the Mishnah, source sheet, or worksheet.
Add close-up detail shots: hands on the sefer, finger following Hebrew words, pencil notes, page turn, or chavrusa exchange.
Use a slow push-in on the speaker or learner when the idea becomes personal or important.
Use reaction shots sparingly: listening face, thinking pause, small nod, or question being asked.
End with a clean closing frame that can hold title, CTA, or source-sheet callout.
negative_prompt_lines: No random camera movement.
No fake cinematic drama that distracts from Torah learning.
No cluttered B-roll that makes the class look staged or stock-like.

patches.title: Calm Lesson Preview Camera Coverage
patches.apply_when: Use for YouTube course library clips, shiur previews, and evergreen lesson content.
prompt_lines: Use a calm two-camera feeling: one medium Rabbi shot and one close source/table shot.
Include one wide orientation shot so the viewer understands the learning setting.
Prefer slow push-in, gentle side angle, and stable tabletop framing.
Let the sefer/source stay visible when the topic depends on the text.
Keep transitions simple: cuts, fades, and light reframes only.
negative_prompt_lines: No whip pans, glitch transitions, heavy zooms, or meme pacing.
No exaggerated rabbi silhouette or anonymous lecture stock look.

patches.title: Source Sheet / Worksheet B-Roll
patches.apply_when: Use when the output supports worksheets, source sheets, question digests, or mekoros.
prompt_lines: Focus the camera language on the learning artifacts.
Use close-ups of a source sheet, Hebrew/English side-by-side notes, Mishnah text, highlighted words, and a pen marking a key idea.
Show an over-the-shoulder view of a learner reading or answering.
Use one clean top-down table shot for worksheets or source-sheet structure.
Leave a safe blank area for overlay labels such as Source, Question, Review, or Takeaway.
negative_prompt_lines: Do not fabricate readable source-sheet text.
Do not generate fake citations as if they are real.

patches.title: Mishnayos Visual Language
patches.apply_when: Use for core One Time Mishnah Class clips.
prompt_lines: Use authentic Mishnayos/Torah-learning visuals: sefarim, chavrusa table, Hebrew text, source sheets, notes, a learning room, and family/home learning support.
Make the Jewish theme specific through learning artifacts and behavior, not costume or stereotypes.
Use warm natural light, real table texture, paper, pen, shelves of sefarim, and human attention.
When showing Hebrew text, keep it respectful and avoid making fake text the main proof point.
Tie visuals back to Mishnah learning, review, questions, clarity, consistency, and parent/student follow-through.
negative_prompt_lines: No generic shtetl, fantasy Temple, glowing scroll, fake ancient prophecy, or costume-drama imagery.
No disrespectful handling of sefarim.
No full sacred Divine Names in generated decorative text.

patches.title: Family Learning And Parent Trust
patches.apply_when: Use when the video is aimed at parents, family learning, or old customer reactivation.
prompt_lines: Show Torah learning as something that enters the home and family routine.
Use visuals like a parent reviewing a worksheet, a boy preparing a question, a father-son table moment, or a family looking at a class resource.
Keep the mood practical and trustworthy rather than sentimental.
Emphasize continuity, review, clarity, and a parent knowing what the child is learning.
negative_prompt_lines: Do not overpromise family transformation.
Do not make the parent look incompetent, shamed, or desperate.

patches.title: Source Sheet / Worksheet Hook
patches.apply_when: Use when a video should lead into source sheets, worksheets, or question digests.
prompt_lines: Include a visual or caption hook that this class has a source sheet, worksheet, or question review path.
Show the learning moving from Rabbi explanation to source review to student action.
If the source sheet is not yet produced, say review sheet, worksheet, or source support without naming exact sources.
Keep the callout short: Learn it, review it, bring a question, or use the worksheet.
negative_prompt_lines: Do not claim that a specific source sheet exists unless it exists.
Do not show source links or citations that were not provided.

patches.title: Ad Candidate Hook
patches.apply_when: Use when the clip may become a paid ad or retargeting creative.
prompt_lines: Open with a concrete parent-facing tension or promise of clarity, not a vague slogan.
Make the first 2 seconds understandable without sound.
Use one clear idea, one visual proof point, and one soft CTA.
Keep the CTA appropriate for One Time: watch the Mishnah class, join the list, ask about the library, or request details.
Leave pricing, launch dates, and guarantee language out unless supplied.
negative_prompt_lines: No fear-based marketing.
No exaggerated guarantee that a child will love learning or change behavior.
No unapproved prices or membership tiers.

patches.title: AI Video Negative Prompt
patches.apply_when: Always for AI-generated or AI-assisted visual prompts.
prompt_lines: Negative prompt: avoid fake Hebrew gibberish as readable source text, inaccurate sefer titles, fantasy Jewish imagery, stock-looking costumes, overdramatic lighting, sacred-name decoration, private student likenesses, cartoon rabbis, exaggerated emotion, and any claim not supplied in the source context.
Keep visuals grounded, respectful, contemporary, and practical.
negative_prompt_lines: fake Hebrew text
invented citations
generic religious stock footage
Temple/fantasy visuals
private child likenesses
guaranteed outcomes
